n: Woe to those who lie awake plotting how to cheat others, then carry it out at dawn simply because they have the power to.

f.w: it is in the power of their hand
f.g: They do it because they can.

n: Powerful landowners seize fields and houses from ordinary families. In Israel land was a family’s God-given inheritance, so this robbed future generations too.

f.g: Inheritance — the family land God promised could never be permanently sold.

n: The schemers have “devised” evil; now God devises disaster for them. They will wear a yoke they cannot shake off and will no longer walk proudly.

f.g: The same word as “devise iniquity” in verse 1 — God answers their plans with His own.
Escape the yoke — slip your necks out of it.

n: Their enemies will mock them with a song of lament: “We are ruined! He has handed our fields over to traitors!” The land-grabbers will lose their land.

f.g: To an apostate or a captor.

n: No one in their family will be left to receive a share when the land is divided again by lot.
The people tell the true prophets, “Don’t preach! Don’t talk about these things — disgrace won’t overtake us.”

f.g: Literally “drip” or “drool” — a scornful word for preaching.

n: Micah answers: Has the Lord’s patience run out? Is this what He wants? God’s words do bless those who live uprightly.

f.w: do not my words do good

n: Lately God’s own people act like enemies, stripping the coats off peaceful travelers who feel safe.

f.g: Returning from war, or peaceable — not expecting attack.

n: They evict widows and mothers from their homes and rob children of their God-given inheritance forever.

f.g: The blessing and dignity God gave them — their place in the land.

n: “Get out! This is no place of rest.” The oppressors who drove others out will themselves be driven out, because their sin has polluted the land.
If a liar came preaching about wine and beer, he’d be just the prophet these people want. People prefer messengers who tell them what they want to hear.

f.w: I will prophesy unto thee of wine and of strong drink

n: A sudden turn to hope: God will gather the remnant of Israel like sheep into a fold. Latter-day Saints see this as part of the promised gathering of Israel.

f.w: I will surely gather the remnant of Israel

f.g: An Edomite region famous for sheep.

n: “The breaker” — one who breaks through barriers — leads the flock out through the gate, with their King and the Lord at their head. Many Christians see Christ as this Shepherd-King who opens the way.

f.g: One who breaks open a way, like a shepherd breaking through the fold wall.

f.w: their king shall pass before them
